title: First authoritative tick responsibility in Rust: the WorldServer pending-block-tick scheduler

provenance.config: composed runtime: light ON_EXPERIMENTAL + worldRegistry + chunkStateAuthority + regionWrite/Read ON + packetAuthority + directNetty + capture session + tickAuthorityMode

ownership.responsibility: WorldServer pending-block-tick scheduler (ScheduledTickUpdate queue, func_175654_a admission / func_72955_a drain)
rust_owns: persistent per-dimension queue state (BTreeMap keyed by (time, priority, seq) = NextTickListEntry.compareTo, ground-truthed from notch bytecode)
admission decisions: (pos, block) dedup (vanilla hashSet.contains equivalent); absolute scheduledTime = totalWorldTime + delay (deterministic, no jitter)
eligibility: scheduledTime <= totalWorldTime (INCLUSIVE; runAllPending drops the predicate)
per-call drain cap: min(queue, 65536) (the 65536 constant is a COUNT cap, not a time horizon — memory said otherwise, bytecode settled it)
drain ordering and removal; collect-then-execute (vanilla drains all eligible before executing any, so same-call re-schedules never re-execute)
drop-on-stale decision (material==AIR or block-changed: consume, no requeue)
java_executes: Block.updateTick (func_180650_b) — all vanilla+mod block behavior fires from Java
updateBlockTick's vanilla body — maintains the Java TreeSet/HashSet mirror (save-side getPendingBlockUpdates -> chunk NBT TileTicks; mod reads stay byte-identical)
unloaded-area requeue via scheduleUpdate(pos, block, 0) (vanilla offsets 349-361)
ownership.displaced_java_branch: WorldServer.tickUpdates' cleaning + ticking loop never executes in ON mode (head hook returns the vanilla semantic result via the LAST_HANDLED handshake)
ownership.displacement_proof: m3a-on14: with the executor fail-closed per entry (FoamFix state-class resolution failure, pre-fix), the falling-sand probe froze at its origin (CONFIRM m3a_sand_pending) — the vanilla loop did not rescue it; nothing else executes ticks when the authority handles and declines
ownership.rust_implementation: crates/native-chunk/src/tick_scheduler.rs (BTreeMap queue + dedup set; 5 unit tests incl. compareTo order, inclusive horizon, count cap, adopt re-seq + collision guard); JNI: crates/ffi/src/native_chunk.rs tickEnqueue/tickDrain/tickAdopt/tickPendingCount/tickClear
ownership.ground_truth_method: javap on notch oo.a(Z)Z / oo.a(Let;Laow;II)V / anf (minecraft_server.1.12.2.jar from the m3a-on12 campaign server) + symbol-index SRG verification of every reflected member

on_run_m3a_on17.scenario: m3a_scheduled_ticks 2/2 confirmed (CONFIRM m3a_water_flow + CONFIRM m3a_sand_resting): flowing water spread and sand fell THROUGH the Rust-owned decision loop

shadow_reference_m3a_shadow6.design: SHADOW = isolated decision comparison: the queue is rebuilt FROM the mirror every call (queue := tree exactly), Rust's drain order/count compared against the vanilla TreeSet decision (first min(size,65536) entries with time <= now in compareTo order), never executed, no double effects/RNG
shadow_reference_m3a_shadow6.scenario: sand_resting confirmed under vanilla execution (behavior parity with ON arm)

shadow_iteration_evidence: shadow4 (restore-drained-batch design): 5570 compares / 1824 count+order mismatches — the vanilla body executes and drains the tree each tick while a restore leaves Rust holding stale entries
shadow5 (rebuild-after-compare): 6335 / 83 — residual = time-only drift on re-scheduled entries (count-equal adopt fast path cannot see it)

compatibility.census: no WorldServer mixins in the 219-mod pack; tickUpdates overridden only in mod wrapper worlds (EnderIO PickupWorld, JustEnoughResources DummyWorld, MCMultiPart MCMPWorldWrapper) that do not touch the WorldServer queue; mods funnel through scheduleUpdate -> updateBlockTick (the hooked choke point)
compatibility.foamfix_finding: FoamFix replaces blockstates with pl.asie.foamfix.common.FoamyBlockState: its DECLARED type is still IBlockState but the concrete class's direct interfaces do not expose it. Parameter-type matching for Block.updateTick must take the signature from Block's own declared methods; a live-class getMethod misses (on14: NoSuchMethodException on every entry, named by the per-path counter). updateTick invoked reflectively against the declared IBlockState parameter accepts the FoamyBlockState instance (assignable)
vanilla_semantics_pinned_from_bytecode: admission gate isBlockLoaded(pos) (func_175667_e): no entry when the chunk is not loaded
scheduledUpdatesAreImmediate (field_72999_e) short-circuit: inline execution / delay=1 / abort — hook skips enqueue and heals via mirror rebuild
AIR-material quirk: entry admitted with scheduledTime=0, priority=0 (setters skipped)
loaded check in the drain is isAreaLoaded(pos, pos) — TWO BlockPos args (func_175707_a), the constants are add(0,0,0) not the remembered ±8
unloaded -> scheduleUpdate(pos, block, 0) requeue; AIR/block-changed -> silent consume (the reverse of what memory said)
tree/set size assertion ('TickNextTick list out of synch') enforced as a mirror invariant (fail-closed)
compatibility.fail_closed: any Throwable in the native path disables the authority permanently (DISABLED_BY_FAILURE); the vanilla body resumes; already-executed callbacks never re-run; declared divergence: a Throwable INSIDE a mod's updateTick (vanilla crashes via ReportedException) degrades to skip-entry-no-crash with the authority handing control back
